name: Ceres
kind: dwarf planet in the asteroid belt
blurb: The largest object between Mars and Jupiter, about 940 km across. NASA's Dawn spacecraft orbited it from 2015.

name: Pallas
blurb: One of the largest asteroids, about 510 km across, on a steeply tilted orbit.

name: Juno
blurb: The third asteroid ever discovered, found in 1804.

name: Vesta
blurb: The brightest asteroid in the sky, about 525 km across. NASA's Dawn spacecraft orbited it in 2011 and 2012.

name: Hygiea
blurb: The fourth-largest object in the asteroid belt, about 430 km across, and very dark.

name: Uranus
blurb: The seventh planet, tipped on its side. It was the first planet found with a telescope, in 1781.

name: Neptune
blurb: The farthest known planet. In 1846 it was found where mathematics predicted it, from its pull on Uranus.

name: Pluto
blurb: Discovered in 1930 by Clyde Tombaugh, who flipped between two photographs exactly as you just did.

name: Haumea
blurb: An egg-shaped world beyond Neptune that spins once every four hours and has a ring.

name: Makemake
blurb: A bright, icy dwarf planet beyond Neptune, discovered in 2005.

name: Eris
blurb: Almost the size of Pluto and far beyond it. Its discovery in 2005 led astronomers to create the term dwarf planet.
